scenes.voiceover: For most of history, the air we breathe belonged only to Earth.

content.title: Air Beyond Earth
content.subtitle: A small box on Mars changes that.

scenes.voiceover: Oxygen isn't just the stuff we breathe. Rocket propellant depends on oxygen.

content.quote: Oxygen isn't just the stuff we breathe. Rocket propellant depends on oxygen, and future explorers will depend on producing propellant on Mars to make the trip home.
content.title: Jim Reuter, NASA STMD
content.caption: April 21, 2021

scenes.voiceover: One hundred twenty-two grams. Twice the original goal, at ninety-eight percent purity.

content.label: GRAMS OF OXYGEN — FINAL RUN
content.caption: 122g total at 98%+ purity, peaking at 12 g/hour — twice NASA's target.

scenes.voiceover: One metric ton for breathing. Twenty-five metric tons to lift off.

content.label: TONS — LIFE SUPPORT FOR A YEAR
content.caption: Breathing: 1 ton. Lifting off Mars: 25 tons. That's why local oxygen matters.

scenes.voiceover: Launch. Land. First breath on Mars. Scale it two hundred times. And one day, lift off again.

content.title: The Path to Air on Mars
items: Next — a 200x larger MOXIE, with a 25–30 kW power plant
2030s — breathable air and return-propellant for a crew

scenes.voiceover: Compress thin CO2. Heat it to eight hundred degrees. Split it with solid oxide. Breathe.

content.title: How MOXIE Makes Air
content.description: The toaster-sized unit takes in Martian CO2 and yields 99.6% pure O2.
items: Pull in thin CO2 through a HEPA filter
Compress with a scroll pump to ~1 atmosphere
Heat to ~800°C (1,470°F) inside a solid-oxide cell
Electrolyze CO2 into oxygen ions and carbon monoxide
Release 99.6% pure O2 — vent the rest

scenes.voiceover: A toaster-shaped box just brewed air on another world. The trip home just got a little closer.

content.title: Air on another world.
content.subtitle: MOXIE, Perseverance, and the first breath off-Earth.
